A.explanation: Gravitational pull of the box on the Earth, equal in size and opposite in direction to $W$, acting upward on the Earth.

B.explanation: Contact normal force of the Earth on the box, a different type of force acting on the same object as $W$.

C.explanation: Acts downward on the box in the same direction as $W$, so it cannot be the opposite third-law pair on the other body.

D.explanation: Horizontal force on the box, while the gravitational pair for $W$ must act along the vertical line joining box and Earth.

hints: Notice $W$ is drawn downward on the box - identify which body exerts it and which body it acts on.
Recall a Newton third-law pair must be the same gravitational type but with the bodies swapped and the direction reversed.
Compare the arrows for object acted on and direction: look for an upward gravitational pull acting on the Earth, not a contact force acting on the box.
walkthrough: Identify $W$: it is the gravitational force exerted by the Earth on the box, acting downward on the box toward the centre of the Earth.
State the third-law rule: the pair must be the same type of force, equal in magnitude, opposite in direction, and act on the other interacting body.
Swap the roles: the pair to $W$ must therefore be the gravitational force exerted by the box on the Earth.
It must act on the Earth, directed upward toward the box, along the same vertical line as $W$.
Arrow A shows an upward force acting on the Earth toward the box, while B is the contact force on the box and C and D have wrong direction or line of action. This is option A
